name: Haunted Places
description: Haunted places are locations across the world where paranormal activity — apparitions, unexplained sounds, sensations, or anomalies — is repeatedly reported by independent witnesses over time. They are studied as a form of ghostlore (a sub-genre of folklore) and underpin a substantial global ghost-tourism industry.
full_description: 'Haunted places' is the cross-cultural meta-category of locations where paranormal activity is repeatedly reported. Wikipedia's List of reportedly haunted locations catalogs sites across more than 47 countries, including castles, palaces, asylums and former psychiatric hospitals, prisons and detention sites, hotels, theatres, ships, battlefields, cemeteries, residential buildings, and ordinary roads and bridges. Folklorists treat these reports as a form of ghostlore — a sub-genre of folklore — rather than as evidence of literal entities, but the persistence and convergence of such reports at certain sites has long attracted both popular and scholarly attention. Repeatedly named globally famous examples include Poveglia (Italy), the Tower of London and Edinburgh Castle (UK), the Catacombs of Paris and Sedlec Ossuary (Europe), Bhangarh Fort (India), Aokigahara forest (Japan), Eastern State Penitentiary and Alcatraz (USA), Port Arthur (Tasmania), the S-21/Tuol Sleng museum (Cambodia), and Recoleta Cemetery (Argentina). Modern paranormal investigation organizations and TV programmes use a mix of historical documentation, eyewitness testimony, and sensor-based equipment (EMF meters, audio recorders, infrared cameras), while academic researchers tend to examine the environmental, neurological, and cultural factors — infrasound, electromagnetic fields, expectation, suggestibility, and culturally transmitted narrative — that contribute to haunting experiences. Ghost tourism is now a multi-billion-dollar global industry, with formal ghost tours operating at most of the most famous sites.
origin: Global. Wikipedia's List of reportedly haunted locations covers more than 47 countries across every inhabited continent.

etymology.origin: Old English haunten via Old French hanter ('to frequent, resort to'); a 'haunted place' is one that ghosts are said to frequent.
etymology.meaning: A location where ghosts or other paranormal phenomena are repeatedly reported.
etymology.first_use: The application of 'haunted' to ghosts is attested in English from at least the 16th century.

timeline.event: Pliny the Younger writes to Lucius Licinius Sura describing a haunted house in Athens (the Athenodorus story), one of the earliest preserved Western haunted-house narratives
timeline.significance: Establishes a literate Western tradition of haunted-place reportage

timeline.event: Hydesville rappings — the Fox sisters' alleged communications begin, catalyzing modern Spiritualism in the United States
timeline.significance: Launches the modern Spiritualist era, in which haunted houses become central cultural objects

timeline.event: Ghost Hunters (TAPS) premieres on Sci Fi Channel
timeline.significance: Launches the modern television ghost-investigation genre and amplifies many haunted-place legends
